issues: No measurement circumvention: the change only swaps binary Morgan bits for count Morgan fingerprints and swaps Tanimoto for the MinMax (generalized Jaccard) kernel. No file access, no pasted answers, no test labels used.

MinMax implementation looks correct: sum_k (A>=k)(B>=k)^T gives sum_i min(a_i, b_i), and na + nb - inter gives sum_i max(a_i, b_i) when na and nb are count sums. The tail of the function is unchanged and still computes inter/(na+nb-inter). The kernel stays positive semi-definite, so the downstream kernel method stays valid.
Recomputed z: (0.4830-0.4804)/(0.0070*sqrt(2)) = 0.26. That matches the harness's 0.255 within rounding of the reported means.
The gain of about 0.0026 is well under the noise sd of 0.0070, with n=1 on each side. 'Reject' is consistent with the numbers. A replicate would be needed to tell whether count/MinMax actually helps.
Minor cost note: the loop runs up to the max count per bit, often 10-30+ iterations of n×n matmuls. That is fine at n≈970 but adds runtime compared with plain Tanimoto.
